vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-66046
vulnerability.description: libexpat1 2.8.3-1~deb13u1: quadratic CPU consumption in storeAtts() (xmlparse.c) when a document specifies many attributes with non-normalized values, each of which triggers a linear scan of the element type's default attributes. Affects Expat through 2.8.3; fixed in Debian at 2.9.0-1~deb13u1.

statements.impact_statement: The trigger is the process parsing attacker-supplied XML with the vulnerable library: a few megabytes of well-formed XML carrying many non-normalized attributes drives O(N^2) work in storeAtts(). The copy flagged here is never loaded, and the one expat that is loaded (CPython's bundled 2.8.5) is past the fix, since the advisory bounds the affected range at 2.8.3. The flagged binary package is Debian libexpat1 2.8.3-1~deb13u1, which provides /usr/lib/<triplet>/libexpat.so.1 and libexpatw.so.1 and enters only through the runtime base nvcr.io/nvidia/distroless/python:3.13-v4.1.7@sha256:fb9e31d8c186ea58c191817c97d945c98f2c39989e7a0643b6384738c1034140: scanning that base alone with grype 0.118.0 (the scan-action pin), --only-fixed -c .grype.yaml, reproduces exactly the five libexpat1 HIGH rows on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, so no AICR-authored layer contributes them. Nothing in the image loads that library. Reading the dynamic section of every ELF file in the aiperf-bench image built at e898b8d58 (index sha256:a8356af256e7530d0534559c65945f790cc2385aaff8789cffd6d0be4f8c5e6e; 717 ELF files on linux/amd64, 713 on linux/arm64) finds no DT_NEEDED entry for libexpat.so.1 or libexpatw.so.1; apart from the library itself the only reference is /etc/ld.so.cache, and no Python source under /opt/venv or /usr/local/lib/python3.13 opens it through ctypes. CPython does not use the system library for XML: lib-dynload/pyexpat.cpython-313-<triplet>.so is built on CPython's bundled expat (pyexpat.EXPAT_VERSION is expat_2.8.5) and its only DT_NEEDED entries are libc.so.6 (plus ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 on arm64), and _elementtree reaches expat only through pyexpat's C-API capsule. A native linux/arm64 run of that image which imported all 1004 aiperf modules and then parsed a document with xml.etree.ElementTree had pyexpat mapped and no libexpat.so.1 in /proc/self/maps. The only XML importer on that import graph is matplotlib 3.11.2's font_manager, which imports plistlib at module load and calls plistlib.loads only from _get_macos_fonts when sys.platform is darwin; aiperf 0.13.0 itself imports none of xml, pyexpat, plistlib or xmlrpc. AICR runs the image only as `aiperf profile --model <text-LLM> --url <endpoint> --endpoint-type chat ...` from buildAIPerfJob in validators/performance/inference_perf_constraint.go, against a cluster-internal http://<svc>.<ns>.svc:<port> endpoint built by resolveFrontendEndpoint / resolveGatewayEndpoint, and exchanges JSON and server-sent events with it, not XML. No bump remediates: Debian fixes at 2.9.0-1~deb13u1, and 3.13-v4.1.7 (built 2026-10-11, digest unchanged on 2026-10-19) is the newest NGC distroless python 3.13 tag and still carries 2.8.3-1~deb13u1 on both architectures; the 3.12 and 3.14 series also end at v4.1.7. So this is a VEX case rather than a base-image bump until NGC rebuilds on the fixed trixie package.

vulnerability.name: CVE-2026-77214
vulnerability.description: libexpat1 2.8.3-1~deb13u1: heap buffer over-read in XML_ParseBuffer (xmlparse.c), which advances m_bufferEnd by a caller-supplied len without checking it against the space left in the parse buffer. Fixed upstream by libexpat commit 13c5f63 (PR #1393, merged 2026-09-25, first released in 2.9.0) and in Debian at 2.9.0-1~deb13u1.

statements.impact_statement: Unlike the other libexpat1 findings, document content alone cannot trigger this one: the embedding application has to call XML_ParseBuffer with a len larger than the unoccupied capacity it obtained from XML_GetBuffer, and the fix is a bounds check on that argument. The copy flagged here is never loaded. CPython's bundled expat 2.8.5 predates the fix (13c5f63 is not an ancestor of R_2_8_5), but CPython never passes an oversized len. Its only XML_ParseBuffer call, in pyexpat.xmlparser.ParseFile (reached from plistlib.load), calls XML_GetBuffer(parser, 2048) on every iteration and passes the length returned by readinst(), which raises ValueError for any read() result longer than the 2048 bytes requested. Every other path goes through XML_Parse, which in expat 2.8.5 calls XML_GetBuffer(parser, len) and then XML_ParseBuffer with that same len. Neither an XML document nor a file object's read() can make len exceed the obtained capacity, so the over-read is unreachable in the bundled copy as well. The flagged binary package is Debian libexpat1 2.8.3-1~deb13u1, which provides /usr/lib/<triplet>/libexpat.so.1 and libexpatw.so.1 and enters only through the runtime base nvcr.io/nvidia/distroless/python:3.13-v4.1.7@sha256:fb9e31d8c186ea58c191817c97d945c98f2c39989e7a0643b6384738c1034140: scanning that base alone with grype 0.118.0 (the scan-action pin), --only-fixed -c .grype.yaml, reproduces exactly the five libexpat1 HIGH rows on linux/amd64 and linux/arm64, so no AICR-authored layer contributes them.
